scope: Prove the first-run resume import path gives the user an explicit opportunity to inspect, verify, and approve extracted career facts before the profile is considered reviewed; imported facts remain pending by default and approval persists across readback and reload. This evidence covers MJ-REQ-251 only.

environment.frontend: local Chromium connected to the application
environment.delivery: local-only; no push or hosted automation

acceptance: A synthetic resume-derived fact enters the profile with verified=false and user_approved=false.
The first-run wizard marks review as needing attention and its Review facts action opens the persisted fact.
The user can explicitly verify and approve the fact; profile API readback confirms both flags persisted.
After browser reload, first-run review shows complete only after the persisted approval.
The connected flow exposes no application submission action and emits no external application or source requests.

checks.evidence: 52 passed; 7 subtests passed, including connected Chromium coverage.
TypeScript and Vite production build passed; existing advisory bundle-size warning remains.
Test module compiles and patch whitespace validation passed.

not_run: Full Python repository suite and PostgreSQL persistence acceptance.
Hosted Actions and hosted review (disabled by local-only policy).
limitations: This evidence proves the user review opportunity and persisted approval gate; it does not claim the broader first-run wizard requirement or the end-to-end product workflow is complete.
